lines: A screen reader should hear what changes, once. Not a clock, every second.
As a step starts, the rider hears it once, in the card's own words: work, round one of eight, thirty seconds at level twenty-four.
When Results opens, it says the result: you finished in twenty-six thirty-eight, and the XP earned.
A dialog takes the focus and keeps it. The app behind it goes inert, and closing gives the focus back to what opened it.
With reduced motion, nothing moves but a fade. The interval bar kept sliding; now it jumps to its place.
Every screen is checked for motion on every run, beside the steps, the result and the dialog.
Results, from a phone to the full screen.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
